quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

60 Questions • Passing Score 50

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead curves only to the right.
The road ahead turns sharply to the right.
The road ahead curves to the right, then to the left.
The road ahead curves to the left, then to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead curves to the right, then to the left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to dangerous conditions ahead. They are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that the road curves right and then left.

questions.question: How do stopping distances and collision severity change with speed?

options.text: They are not affected by speed.

questions.explanation: High speed is dangerous. As speed increases, the impact of a crash gets worse, causing more serious injuries and deaths. Leave more space between you and other cars as you speed up so you can stop safely if needed.

questions.question: At night, an oncoming car has high beams on and you cannot see the road. What should you do?

options.text: Look toward the left edge of your lane.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.
Look straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at the headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of your lane and watch the other car from the corner of your eye.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a low overhead clearance. Do not proceed if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign (13 feet 6 inches in this case).

questions.question: A steady yellow light means what color light will come next?
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a steady red light will appear next.

questions.question: Must you always stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road?
questions.explanation: You must always stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road, no matter which direction you are traveling. Be careful around children.

questions.question: You are on a one-way street and an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches. What must you do?

options.text: Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights or siren approaches on a one-way street, drive to the nearest roadside and stop.

questions.question: When is passing prohibited?
questions.explanation: It is illegal and unsafe to pass on hills, curves, at intersections, and at railroad crossings.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speeding is safe if you are a skilled driver.
Both "Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."

questions.correctAnswerText: Both "Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."
questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase the risk of death in a crash. At speeds above 80 miles per hour, survival in a crash is unlikely. Driving slower than other traffic is also dangerous because other drivers may become impatient and make risky passing moves.

questions.question: Does your speed affect how far your vehicle travels after you brake?
questions.explanation: Speed greatly affects braking distance. As you drive faster, the distance your vehicle needs to stop increases. Always leave plenty of space between you and the car in front of you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for traffic on your right.

questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this intersection.

questions.question: What are blind spots?

options.text: Areas where your vision gets blurry when you are tired.
Areas around your vehicle that you cannot see in your mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas around your vehicle that you cannot see in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas near the rear corners of your vehicle that your mirrors cannot show. When changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check these spots.

questions.question: Airbags provide full protection during a crash.
questions.explanation: Airbags inflate during a front-end crash and provide extra protection. However, you must also wear your safety belt to get full protection in a crash.

questions.question: When should you drive at the maximum posted speed limit?
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the fastest speed allowed under perfect conditions. Always drive at a safe speed based on weather, traffic, and road conditions. Adjust your speed to match traffic and stay safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road becomes slippery when it rains or is wet.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line in the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. You cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. You can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. You cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction. You can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions. You cannot pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A solid line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Get ready for traffic to merge into your lane from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get ready for traffic to merge into your lane from the right.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you that traffic will merge from the right into your lane. Be prepared to let them in safely.

questions.question: You are in a left turn lane at an intersection with oncoming traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the left of the center lane.
Signal before you reach the intersection.
Turn your wheels left while waiting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal before you reach the intersection.
questions.explanation: Signal about 100 feet before you turn. Keep your wheels straight until it is safe to turn. This way, if another car hits you from behind, you won't be pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What is distracted driving?

options.text: Anything that causes you to swerve.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving means anything that pulls your eyes, hands, or mind away from driving. It is a major cause of crashes. Distractions prevent you from seeing and hearing important warnings.

questions.question: Why is it important to look far ahead while driving on the highway?

options.text: It helps you keep up with other traffic.
It reduces sudden braking and sharp turns.
It lets you spot police officers.

questions.correctAnswerText: It reduces sudden braking and sharp turns.
questions.explanation: Looking ahead helps you see hazards early. You can plan ahead and avoid sudden stops or turns. This makes driving safer, saves fuel, and keeps traffic moving smoothly.

questions.question: What is a good rule for passing other vehicles?

options.text: Pass on the right whenever possible.
Drive with traffic flow and pass only when necessary.
Move to the front of slow traffic so you can see better.
Always flash your lights and honk to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with traffic flow and pass only when necessary.
questions.explanation: Each time you pass another vehicle, there is a greater risk of a crash. If you drive faster than surrounding traffic, you will need to keep passing others. Drive at the speed of traffic, obey the speed limit, and pass only when needed.

questions.question: What does excessive speed lead to?

options.text: It does not increase crash risk.
It helps you react faster to danger.

questions.explanation: Excessive speed causes many vehicle crashes. Driving too fast does not save time and often leads to unsafe decisions.

questions.question: How should small children ride in a vehicle?

options.text: A strong adult can safely hold them.
They are safe standing on the floor in the back.
They will not get hurt in a crash because they are small.
They must never stand while the vehicle is moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: They must never stand while the vehicle is moving.
questions.explanation: Special child seats are made for small children. No person is strong enough to hold a child safely during a crash or sudden stop. Always keep children properly secured in a seat.

questions.question: Is it true that talking or texting on a cell phone while driving does not increase crash risk?
questions.explanation: Using a phone while driving takes your attention away from the road and increases your crash risk.

questions.question: Where should your car be positioned when making a right turn?

options.text: Near the center of the street.
Close to the left side of the street.
Close to the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Before making a right turn, move as far to the right side of the road as possible. Do not cut across traffic lanes when turning.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed on wet roads.
Keep tires at the correct air pressure.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your vehicle slides on water between the tires and road. Low tire pressure or worn tread increases hydroplaning risk. Speeding also makes it worse.

questions.question: If someone is injured in an accident, what should you do?

options.text: Move the injured person away immediately.
Do not move them unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move them unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move injured people unless there is danger. Moving them incorrectly can make minor injuries worse. Keep them warm until help arrives. If there is heavy bleeding, apply direct pressure to stop it.

questions.question: What provides the best protection in a crash?

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
questions.explanation: Safety belts double your chances of surviving a crash and reduce serious injury. Airbags work best with safety belts in front-end crashes. Wear both your lap and shoulder belt.

questions.question: What problems do worn or bald tires cause?

options.text: They are more likely to hydroplane.

questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires increase stopping distance and make turning harder. Tires without good tread also increase hydroplaning risk.

questions.question: When should you yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk?

options.text: Only if they wave at you.
Only if they are not texting.

questions.explanation: Stop completely at a crosswalk to let pedestrians cross. You can only go if no one is in the crosswalk or intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This three-sided sign warns you to slow down at an intersection. Be ready to stop and let other drivers and pedestrians go first. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: You have a green light and there are pedestrians in the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: You have the right-of-way over pedestrians.
Pedestrians must wait for you to cross.

questions.explanation: Even with a green light, you must let pedestrians and other vehicles already in the intersection go first. Always yield to pedestrians when turning on a green light.

questions.question: Before driving, you must remove snow, frost, and ice from:

options.text: Just the windshield and passenger window.

questions.explanation: You need to see clearly out of all windows before you drive. Clean all windows, mirrors, and lights of snow, ice, and frost.

questions.question: Drivers do not have to yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk.
questions.explanation: You must stop completely and yield to pedestrians in marked crosswalks. You must also yield to pedestrians in unmarked crosswalks on your side of the road when there are no traffic signals.

questions.question: At a crosswalk, who must yield?

options.text: Construction workers must yield to you.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crossings if they obey traffic signals. If there is no traffic signal, you must stop for pedestrians in any crosswalk, marked or unmarked.

questions.question: When can a driver legally pass on the right?

options.text: If the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane.
Even if it means driving off the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane.
questions.explanation: You may pass on the right if there is an extra lane and the car ahead is turning left or waiting to turn left. You can also pass on the right on roads with two or more lanes in the same direction. Never drive off the road to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: Which statement about driving speed is true?

options.text: As your speed increases, the chance of a fatality increases.
As your speed increases, so should your following distance.

questions.explanation: Higher speeds make crashes more deadly. At speeds over 80 miles per hour, survival in a crash is unlikely. As you go faster, you need more distance between your car and the car in front of you to stop safely.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and alert you to upcoming hazards. This sign warns of a steep hill. Slow down to avoid crashes and brake damage.

questions.question: You approach a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Drive around the gates if you don't see a train.
Stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then proceed when the gates are lifted.
Slow down and drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then proceed when the gates are lifted.
questions.explanation: You must stop at railroad crossings when you see warning signs, lights, or flaggers. It is illegal to drive around lowered gates.

questions.question: There is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian can see you before proceeding.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: You must always let pedestrians cross, even without a marked crosswalk. Give them the right-of-way.

questions.question: Before you enter an intersection, you should look to your:
questions.explanation: Before entering an intersection, look left and right for vehicles and pedestrians. Look left a second time because vehicles from your left will be closer. Check across the whole intersection to make sure it is clear before you move.

questions.question: To avoid being in a truck or bus driver's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Avoid driving alongside them and avoid tailgating.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving alongside them and avoid tailgating.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have large blind spots on their sides and rear. Do not drive next to them and do not drive too close behind them.

questions.question: Signs with orange backgrounds are:
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn you about construction and maintenance work ahead.

questions.question: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across traffic lanes:
questions.explanation: Stop lines are solid white lines at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks. They show exactly where you must stop.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that traffic only moves in one direction. You must drive in the direction the sign points.

questions.question: When you hear the siren or see the flashing lights of an approaching emergency vehicle, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Motion for the emergency vehicle to pass you.
Merge into the right lane and continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using flashing lights or a siren. Move to the right side of the road and stop until it passes. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then stop on the right side.

questions.question: A red arrow displayed on a traffic light means that:

options.text: A driver must proceed slowly through the intersection.
A driver must stop and then proceed when the way is clear.
A driver must stop and then proceed when the signal changes to a green light or green arrow.
A driver may turn in the direction that the red arrow is pointing.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver must stop and then proceed when the signal changes to a green light or green arrow.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must stop completely. You can only move when a green light or green arrow appears.

questions.question: Collisions are more likely to happen when:

options.text: All vehicles are traveling at about the same speed.
One lane of traffic is traveling faster than the other lanes.
One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Collisions happen more often when one vehicle drives faster or slower than other vehicles. Driving faster than traffic increases your crash risk. Driving slower can cause rear-end collisions or make other drivers swerve to avoid you.

questions.question: An orange-colored sign like this means:
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn you about construction ahead. Drive carefully.

questions.question: A flashing red light on a traffic signal means:

options.text: The same thing as a stop sign.
You do not have to come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop, just like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: You are driving at the speed limit when the traffic light turns yellow. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and go through the intersection without stopping.
Speed up to cross before the light turns red.
Stop before the intersection if you can do so safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before the intersection if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming soon. You should stop if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, you may cross the intersection with caution.

questions.question: As you drive up a hill, what should you do?

options.text: Be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: You cannot see what is on the other side of a hill. A vehicle could be stopped just out of sight. You must be able to stop if necessary. Slow down when approaching hills or curves.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and taking action to prevent accidents.
Dealing with bad drivers by passing them in traffic.
Following the car in front of you closely.
Changing lanes quickly to get through traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and taking action to prevent accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you recognize unsafe situations and act before an accident happens. It helps you avoid crashes with dangerous, careless, or drunk drivers and pedestrians.

questions.question: What does an octagonal sign always mean?
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign is always a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop at a red, eight-sided sign.

questions.question: Solid lines between traffic lanes mean you cannot pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: Solid lines show areas where passing is not safe. Dashed lines show areas where you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs tell you?

options.text: The fastest or slowest speed you are allowed to drive.
The speed to drive in heavy traffic.
The speed to drive in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fastest or slowest speed you are allowed to drive.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the highest and lowest safe speeds allowed on the road. The maximum speed is for perfect conditions. You must drive slower when conditions are bad.

questions.question: After a school bus stops to let children off, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until the children wave to you before moving.
Watch for children walking on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking on the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After stopping for a school bus with the stop arm out and lights flashing, watch for children on the sides of the road. Always drive carefully around children.

questions.question: Car drivers should know that large trucks:

options.text: Do not need extra space to turn and stop.

questions.explanation: Large trucks have blind spots in front, on the sides, and in back. Stay out of these areas. Trucks need more space to turn and stop than cars because of their size and weight.

questions.question: Even a small amount of alcohol can affect a driver's:
questions.explanation: Any amount of alcohol can affect your ability to drive safely. Even a small amount hurts your judgment and physical coordination. Driving after drinking any alcohol can result in criminal charges.

questions.question: If you stop on the road at night, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on your hazard lights and keep your low beams on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your hazard lights and keep your low beams on.
questions.explanation: When you stop on the road at night, turn on your hazard lights and keep your low beam headlights on. This makes sure other drivers can see your vehicle clearly.
